title: Dwarf Galaxy Holmberg IX
caption: Dwarf irregular galaxy Holmberg IX, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: Holmberg IX, UGC 5336 · constellation Ursa Major · about 12 million light-years away (source figure)
credit: NASA, ESA, and the Hubble Heritage Team (STScI/AURA); Acknowledgment: D. de Mello (Catholic University of America and GSFC)

recognition.text: NASA Hubble image release (STScI). No published audience rating.

story: Blue, white and red stars and distant galaxies scatter across a black background, with an irregular, denser grouping of stars at the centre. That loose gathering is Holmberg IX, a dwarf irregular galaxy sitting just off the outer edge of the large spiral M81, 12 million light-years away in Ursa Major.

Hubble resolves more than 20,000 individual stars in the picture. Only about 10 percent are old stars, billions of years in age, while the others are thought to be young, between 10 and 200 million years old. The old and young stars are spread out differently, which may relate to how they formed. Holmberg IX itself is suspected to be a product of an interaction between M81 and its neighbour M82.

Simulations suggest M81, M82 and nearby NGC 3077 passed close to one another 200 to 300 million years ago, and that encounter may have set off the newer star formation. Many small nearby galaxies form stars, but none is as dominated by young stars as Holmberg IX.

understand.summary: A composite of two exposures from Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys. F555W is shown in cyan and F814W in orange.
understand.eye: The F814W filter records near-infrared light the eye cannot see, and the colours are assigned to two separate filter images.

explore: Holmberg IX is a Magellanic-type galaxy, similar in size and irregular structure to the Small Magellanic Cloud. Sidney van den Bergh discovered it in 1959 and catalogued it as DDO 66, and it took its present name from Eric Holmberg's study of galaxy groups ten years later. Astronomers hope it will show how such dwarfs act as building blocks of large galaxies.
